description: Temperate fruit tree grown in India mainly in Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. It needs winter chilling, so in the plains and in Andhra Pradesh / Telangana only low-chill varieties such as Anna and HRMN-99 are tried.
npk_split: For trees 10 years and older: apply FYM with all P and K in December-January, half the N 2-3 weeks before flowering and the rest a month later.

Black rot.name: Black Rot
Black rot.description: Fungal disease that causes 'frog-eye' leaf spots, a firm black fruit rot and cankers on limbs. The fungus lives in dead wood and mummified fruits and builds up in poorly pruned orchards.
symptoms: Small purple specks on leaves that grow into round spots with a tan centre and purple-brown border (frog-eye)
Badly spotted leaves turn yellow and fall early
Firm brown to black rot starting at the blossom end of the fruit
Rotted fruits dry into black mummies that stay on the tree
Sunken, cracked, reddish-brown bark (canker) on limbs
Black rot.spread: Rain splashes spores from cankers, dead wood and mummified fruits onto leaves, fruits and wounds in warm wet weather.
Black rot.action: Prune out cankered and dead wood, remove all mummified fruits and protect new growth with a fungicide spray after petal fall.

treatment.name: Canker pruning and removal of mummified fruits
treatment.notes: Cut back to healthy wood during dry weather and burn the prunings.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP paste or Bordeaux paste
treatment.notes: Seal every large cut the same day.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: From petal fall at 14-day intervals in wet weather.

Cedar apple rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Cedar apple rust.description: Rust disease that needs both apple and juniper (cedar) trees to complete its life cycle. It is a North American disease not known to be established in India, so have the diagnosis confirmed before spraying.
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange round spots on the upper leaf surface, often with a red border
Tiny black dots in the centre of the spots
Small pale tube-like tufts under the spots on the leaf underside
Heavily spotted leaves turn yellow and drop
Similar orange spots on young fruits
Cedar apple rust.spread: Wind carries spores from galls on juniper trees to apple leaves in wet spring weather; it does not spread from apple to apple.
Cedar apple rust.action: Get the diagnosis confirmed by the horticulture officer and remove juniper (cedar) hosts close to the orchard.

treatment.name: Removal of juniper (cedar) hosts near the orchard
treatment.notes: Breaks the life cycle; the rust cannot survive on apple alone.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Protective sprays from pink bud until 3-4 weeks after petal fall.

treatment.name: Myclobutanil 10 WP
treatment.notes: Registered on apple for scab; the same sprays also check rust.

Scab.name: Apple Scab
Scab.description: The most damaging fungal disease of apple in Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh, attacking leaves and fruits in cool, wet springs. Scabbed fruits crack, stay small and lose market value.
symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves
Spotted leaves pucker, turn yellow and fall early
Dark, rough, corky scabs on fruits
Scabbed fruits are misshapen and crack
Scab.spread: Spores released from last year's fallen leaves infect new leaves in spring rain and then spread from spot to spot by rain splash.
Scab.action: Start protective fungicide sprays at green tip to pink bud stage and repeat every 10-14 days while the weather stays wet.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Protectant; from green tip / pink bud stage at 10-14 day intervals.

treatment.name: Difenoconazole 25 EC
treatment.notes: At petal fall and fruit set; not more than 2 sprays a season.

treatment.name: Urea 5% spray on leaves before leaf fall
treatment.notes: Speeds up rotting of fallen leaves that carry the fungus; also collect and burn fallen leaves.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or deficiency. Keep following the regular orchard spray and nutrition schedule.
symptoms: Uniform green leaves without spots or powdery growth
No curling, puckering or early leaf fall
healthy.spread: Not applicable - no disease or pest detected.
healthy.action: Continue regular pruning, balanced manuring and weekly scouting of the orchard.
